fix(transformer): subtract cache tokens from input_tokens to match Anthropic spec (#33)

* fix(transformer): subtract cache tokens from input_tokens

Per Anthropic Messages API spec, the `input_tokens` field counts only
regular input tokens — tokens that were neither read from the cache nor
written to the cache during this turn. OpenAI's `prompt_tokens` is the
*total* prompt size. The current 1:1 mapping double-counts cached
tokens as both `input_tokens` and `cache_read_input_tokens` /
`cache_creation_input_tokens`.

Symptom: when a Claude Code client uses oc-go-cc with a long-prefix
workload (system prompt + MCP tool definitions + CLAUDE.md + tools
output), the harness reads `input_tokens` from each response and
treats it as the conversation size for its local auto-compact counter.
Because the proxy reports the full prompt size every turn, the harness
trips auto-compact at ~80% of its 200k window in only a handful of
turns, even though the true uncached delta per turn is small.

Empirically observed (deepseek-v4-pro through OpenCode Go):
  call 1: prompt_tokens=4927, cache_hit=0,    cache_miss=4927
  call 2: prompt_tokens=4926, cache_hit=4864, cache_miss=62
After this fix:
  call 1 anthropic input_tokens = 4927 - 0 - 4927 = 0   (all newly cached)
  call 2 anthropic input_tokens = 4926 - 4864 - 62 = 0  (all accounted for)
Before this fix, both calls reported input_tokens=4927/4926, an
~80x inflation on call 2.

Anthropic's spec describes input_tokens as the count excluding cache
reads and writes. With this change, oc-go-cc's mapping matches the
behavior of Anthropic-native providers (verified against Z.AI's
Anthropic-compat endpoint, which also drops input_tokens to ~0 after
caching kicks in on long-prefix sessions).

Includes `nonNegative` helper to clamp the subtraction in case an
upstream payload has cache fields that don't precisely sum to
prompt_tokens. Updates two existing tests that asserted the previous
behavior and adds a new TestTransformResponseWithPartialCacheTokens
for the case where some prompt tokens are neither hit nor miss.

fix(transformer): add reasoning_content placeholder to DeepSeek text-only assistant turns (#34)

* fix(transformer): add reasoning_content placeholder to DeepSeek text-only assistant turns

DeepSeek in thinking mode requires `reasoning_content` on every assistant
message in the conversation history, not just tool_use turns. The current
placeholder logic at request.go:291 gates on `len(toolCalls) > 0`, so a
text-only assistant message inside a thinking-mode conversation gets
ReasoningContent=nil and upstream rejects the entire request:

    API error 400: invalid_request_error
    "The reasoning_content in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API."

How this manifests in practice (real claude-go session, today):

  msg type                         current placeholder?  upstream
  -------------------------------- --------------------  --------
  assistant: thinking + text       no (uses real)        ok
  assistant: thinking + tool_use   no (uses real)        ok
  assistant: tool_use only         YES                   ok
  assistant: text only             NO ← bug              400

Claude Code drops thinking blocks on plenty of legitimate continuation
turns — short follow-up answers, post-/compact summary messages, replies
that don't require chain-of-thought. Each one currently breaks the chain
because the proxy's placeholder gate misses them.

Fix: drop the `len(toolCalls) > 0` constraint so the placeholder is
applied to ALL assistant turns when (a) the conversation has thinking
history and (b) the model is DeepSeek. The Moonshot branch is unchanged
(it has different validator semantics around tool_calls specifically).

* fix(transformer): detect and round-trip thinking content attached to tool_use blocks

Claude Code emits two shapes for assistant turn reasoning:

(1) Dedicated thinking block:
    { "type": "thinking", "thinking": "..." }

(2) Inline on the tool_use block (when the turn ends in a tool call):
    { "type": "tool_use", "id": "...", "name": "...",
      "input": {...}, "thinking": "reasoning that led here" }

The previous code only handled (1). For (2), HasThinkingBlocks returned
false (it only matched type=="thinking") and transformAssistantMessage
ignored the inline thinking field while still emitting the tool_call —
so reasoning_content was nil on the assistant message in the upstream
request. DeepSeek (which defaults to thinking mode after its first
reasoning response) then 400'd:

    The reasoning_content in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API.

This was the actual production failure mode the previous commit's fix
didn't catch: claude-go session repeatedly stalled ("Cooked for 20s",
no output) because the harness was sending tool_use+thinking blocks the
proxy was silently dropping.

Fix:
  - HasThinkingBlocks: also return true for tool_use blocks with a
    non-empty Thinking field.
  - transformAssistantMessage: extract Thinking from tool_use blocks
    into thinkingParts (alongside the existing thinking-typed branch),
    so the tool_call AND the reasoning_content both reach upstream.

Test: TestTransformRequestExtractsThinkingFromToolUseBlock asserts
HasThinkingBlocks detects the inline shape, ReasoningContent carries the
inline thinking string, and the tool_call is still emitted.

* fix(transformer): force-disable thinking mode for DeepSeek without thinking history

This is the actual fix for the production issue. The two earlier
commits in this PR (cb1901b, d0a6dc4) widened reasoning_content
placeholder coverage and broadened tool_use+thinking detection — both
correct hardening but neither sufficient to unblock the live failure
because they assumed the proxy was responsible for *populating*
reasoning_content. The deeper root cause is that DeepSeek-v4 defaults
to thinking mode upstream, and once engaged, demands reasoning_content
on every assistant message in history. The proxy never explicitly
disables it for users with bare model config (no Thinking, no
ReasoningEffort), so:

  turn 1: succeeds (DeepSeek runs in default thinking mode, returns
          reasoning_content which the proxy converts to a thinking block)
  turn 2: Claude Code may not round-trip a non-empty thinking field
          back to the proxy. HasThinkingBlocks returns false. The
          proxy leaves openaiReq.Thinking nil. Upstream is STILL in
          thinking mode (default), demands reasoning_content from the
          prior assistant message that the proxy didn't add → 400:
          "The reasoning_content in the thinking mode must be passed
          back to the API."

Fix: when the model is DeepSeek and there's no extant thinking history,
explicitly send `thinking: {type: "disabled"}` to switch off upstream
thinking mode. Combined with the prior commits, the chain is now:

  - history has thinking → enable thinking + extract real
    reasoning_content (or placeholder for assistant turns where it was
    elided/dropped) — covers both the dedicated thinking-block shape
    and the tool_use+thinking inline shape
  - no thinking history + DeepSeek → force-disable upstream thinking
  - no thinking history + non-DeepSeek with model config asking for
    thinking → unchanged (still force-disable so reasoning_content
    isn't demanded on a nil prior turn)

Verified in production: a real claude-go session that was reliably
400ing on tool-call follow-ups now streams responses correctly
through multi-turn workflows.

Test: TestTransformRequestForceDisablesThinkingForDeepSeekWithoutHistory
constructs a bare DeepSeek model config with no thinking history and
asserts openaiReq.Thinking is set to the explicit-disabled value.

The earlier commits remain useful as defenses-in-depth for the case
where thinking history *does* exist (e.g., a user who explicitly opts
into thinking via model config, or a multi-session workflow that
inherits thinking blocks from a prior conversation).

The previous heuristic routed a request to the vision scenario
whenever the conversation history contained any image AND the
latest user text matched a broad visual-intent keyword list
("image", "screenshot", "screen", "ui", "layout", "visual",
"foto", "vedi", etc.). The intent was to catch "describe this
image" follow-ups without re-attachment.

In practice this fired false positives on ordinary prose that
happens to mention those words — "fix the UI layout", "check
this Docker image", "look at the screenshot of the error",
"resize this image to 1024x1024". For a long-running session

vision_long_context (1M ctx) instead of the originally-requested
model — making each new turn noticeably slower for no benefit.

latest user message actually contains a new (unseen-hash)
image. If a user wants to ask about a previously-attached
image, they should re-attach it; the routing decision should
be based on what the latest request actually contains, not
on ambiguous keyword matching against stale history.

while its own profile, the decision tree and the quick reference all said
1,850. Nothing in the repo can settle it — the model catalog carries no rate
data for any of its 353 models — but the row duplicated GLM-5's figure
exactly, which reads as a copy-paste, and 1,850 is what the other three

* fix(ci): extract RPM payloads with relative paths in verification

The RPM Packaging job failed on ubuntu-latest with "cpio: cannot make
directory '/etc/routatic-proxy': Permission denied". RPM payload members are
absolute paths, and whether cpio strips the leading "/" by default differs
between distributions — Fedora's does, Ubuntu's does not, so the extraction
step aimed at the runner's real /usr and /etc instead of the temp dir.

Passing --no-absolute-filenames makes it explicit rather than relying on the
local default. This is why the job exists: the same script passed on a Fedora
workstation and only failed on a real Linux CI runner.

* fix(ci): judge cpio's status, not rpm2cpio's, when verifying RPMs

Ubuntu's rpm2cpio exits 1 even when it has written the payload in full, while
Fedora's exits 0. Under `set -o pipefail` that sank the whole extraction
pipeline, so the RPM job failed on ubuntu-latest immediately after the
previous fix let cpio run at all.

The status we care about is cpio's, so the pipeline runs with pipefail off and
its subshell status is captured instead. Because that means neither exit code
is fully trusted, the script now also compares the extracted binary's size
against the size recorded in the RPM header — a mid-stream extraction failure
would otherwise leave a truncated binary whose ELF header still looks valid.

Reproduced and fixed against ubuntu:24.04 in a container rather than guessing:
both arches now pass on Ubuntu and Fedora, and the wrong-arch and
wrong-version negative controls still exit 1.

* feat(opencode-go): add OpenAI Responses endpoint support via wire_format config

The Go provider previously only supported Anthropic Messages and OpenAI Chat
Completions endpoints. Models that require the OpenAI Responses API
(muse-spark-1.2-contributor, grok-4.5) could not be used through routatic.

Changes:

  anthropic, responses, gemini), falling back to built-in classification

  (following the same pattern as the existing Zen provider implementation)
- Update `getEndpoint` in legacy client to route Responses models

This is configuration-driven: users add `"wire_format": "responses"`
to their model_overrides to opt any model into the Responses endpoint,
without requiring code changes. No hardcoded model lists are modified.

* fix(opencode-go): make wire_format override authoritative on every dispatch path

Address review findings on #141.

The streaming handler resolved a model's wire format with the Provider
interface method while the provider resolved it with a private helper that
read the wire_format override. For a Go model configured with
`wire_format: "responses"` the provider streamed from /v1/responses while
the handler parsed those bytes as Chat Completions chunks, corrupting the
stream, skipping the heartbeat pause, and mislabelling fallback logs.

Collapse the two resolvers into one so they cannot drift:

- Widen core.Provider.WireFormat to take config.ModelConfig. Execute,
  Stream, and internal/handlers/messages.go now all dispatch on that single
  method. Zen and Bedrock keep classifying by model ID.
- Add core.ParseWireFormat as the only interpreter of wire_format strings,
  and client.GoWireFormat/GoWireFormatFor as the only resolver for Go models.
- Drop "gemini" from the values the Go provider honours. It has no Gemini
  path, so Execute/Stream fell through to default and silently sent a chat
  body to BaseURL.

Also:

- Default opencode_go.responses_base_url to
  https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/responses in applyDefaults, matching the Zen
  equivalent, and guard an explicitly empty value with a named error instead
  of an opaque `unsupported protocol scheme ""` on every fallback attempt.
- Revert the getEndpoint Responses case for Go models. getEndpoint is shared
  by ChatCompletion, ResponsesCompletion and GeminiCompletion and cannot tell
  which body type is being marshalled; the legacy path only dispatches
  Responses for Zen, so that case could only POST a chat body to
  /v1/responses. Comment records why the override is not read there.
- Cover override precedence, alias handling, the ignored "gemini" value, the
  format/endpoint agreement contract, the missing-URL error, and the new
  loader default.
- Document the override and the single-resolution rule in CLAUDE.md, and add
  responses_base_url to the example and template configs.

* fix(config): accept all providers in model and family overrides (#134)

model_overrides and model_family_overrides rejected "openrouter" and
"aws-bedrock" even though models and fallbacks accept them and the
handler dispatches those providers generically through the registry.
The allow-list in validateOverrideMap had simply not kept up with the

Move the canonical provider names, NormalizeProvider and IsKnownProvider
into internal/config — the lowest layer that knows every provider, since

normalization, so "aws_bedrock" resolves identically everywhere.

Closes #134

* fix(update): actionable error for unwritable install dir, same-fs staging

`routatic-proxy update` on a root-owned install path failed with the raw
"cannot back up current binary: rename ...: permission denied", after
downloading the whole asset. Two problems in the install step:

- the staging file was created in the system temp dir, so the final
  rename crossed filesystems whenever /tmp is its own mount (tmpfs on
  most Linux systems) and failed with EXDEV
- permission failures surfaced as raw rename errors with no hint

Stage the download in the install directory instead: the rename is now
same-filesystem and atomic, and creating the staging file first makes an
unwritable location fail before the download rather than after. Wrap
permission failures with the directory and the next step (sudo, or the
package manager the binary came from). Resolve symlinks so a linked
install is replaced at its real path instead of clobbering the link.

Also compare versions with IsNewerVersion rather than string ordering,
which reported v0.6.10 as older than v0.6.9.

* fix(update): resolve beta releases; document the beta channel

The beta channel could never find a release: it matched tags containing
"-beta-", but real beta tags are v{VERSION}-beta.{N} (v0.6.4-beta.5), so
every `update` on the beta channel failed with "no beta releases found".
Match the actual format and pick the highest beta by semantic version
rather than trusting GitHub's publish-date ordering.

Documentation described an update command that does not exist — flags
--check/--yes/--force, checksum verification, and a .old backup all
belong to internal/updater, which was orphaned when the CLI was
rewritten. Correct that surface across INSTALLATION.md, README.md,
docs/fedora-setup.md and the zh translations, and add an end-to-end beta
guide: opting in via update-channel, where the preference is stored, the
Docker `beta` tag, installing a specific prerelease by tag (including the
RPM filename's dotted suffix), and why switching back to stable does not
downgrade. Add update failure modes to TROUBLESHOOTING.md.

* refactor(update): match only the beta tag format the generator emits

Review feedback on #152: isBetaTag still accepted "-beta-" alongside
"-beta.", the very pattern the fix identified as matching no real tag.
get-versions.sh is the only producer of beta tags and emits exactly
v{VERSION}-beta.{N}, and no tag in the repo's history uses the hyphen
form, so the branch was dead. Match the generator literally and assert
the hyphenated spelling is ignored so it cannot creep back.

fix(daemon): preserve Homebrew stable symlink for launchd autostart on macOS (#164)

On macOS, `routatic-proxy autostart enable` wrote the EvalSymlinks-
resolved Cellar/X.Y.Z path into ProgramArguments[0] of
~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.routatic.proxy.plist. Homebrew deletes the
old Cellar on `brew upgrade`/`brew cleanup`, so the plist became
dangling and launchd failed on next login. The running daemon stayed
in RAM via `start --_daemonize` (PPID 1), masking the failure.

Fix: for darwin + Homebrew prefixes (/opt/homebrew, /usr/local),
keep the stable symlink (/opt/homebrew/bin, /opt/homebrew/opt,
/usr/local/bin, /usr/local/opt) via filepath.Abs instead of
EvalSymlinks to Cellar. All other platforms and non-brew macOS
installs keep current behavior; update symlink resolution unchanged.

Tested: overlaid fixed binary to Cellar/0.6.4, `autostart disable/enable`
now writes /opt/homebrew/bin/routatic-proxy (Cellar count 0), launchctl
loaded, health ok. `brew reinstall` correctly leaves stale Cellar/0.6.3
plist until re-enable — fix makes next enable stable.

feat(opencode): forward Claude Code session ID as x-opencode-session (#166)

OpenCode Go requires an x-opencode-session header (one stable ID per
conversation) or requests may error after 09/06. Claude Code sends the
conversation UUID as x-claude-code-session-id on every /v1/messages
request; forward it verbatim to OpenCode Go so it can group requests by
conversation.

- Resolve the inbound header once in HandleMessages and carry it via
  context (core.WithSessionID / SessionIDFromContext), so it reaches
  every provider call and every fallback attempt.
- Set x-opencode-session in all OpenCode Go request builders (provider
  executeAnthropic/streamAnthropic/doRequest, plus the legacy client's
  ChatCompletion/SendAnthropicRequest/ResponsesCompletion/
  GeminiCompletion).
- Scope: OpenCode Go only. Zen, Bedrock, and OpenRouter are untouched.
- Missing inbound header falls back to a per-request UUID so the
  upstream header is always present.
- Tests cover streaming + non-streaming propagation, same/different
  session stability, UUID fallback, fallback-attempt sharing, and the
  Zen/Bedrock/OpenRouter scope boundary.
